title: Transient capacity event: soft-fence controller to isolate noisy tenant and recalibrate burst-credit slabs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: On 2025-11-09 a dedicated GPU cluster experienced a multi-hour capacity degradation affecting ~12 tenants. Root signals pointed to a single tenant exhibiting sustained tail requests that amplified KV-cache pressure and triggered burst token exhaustion across the pool. Current reservation heuristics allowed transient burst credits to be consumed unevenly, which amplified noisy-neighbor effects.

Incident summary: Between 03:20–06:45 UTC a tenant (redacted customer id) generated an unusual mix of long-sequence generations and high QPS small-sequence calls. This resulted in: (1) KV-cache thrashing on shared nodes, (2) burst credit depletion in the allocator, (3) eviction churn and throttling-induced tail latency for other tenants. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ccp/dedicated-capacity-incident-2025-11-09 (internal). Immediate mitigation: manual soft-quarantine applied to the noisy tenant at 04:10 UTC which reduced cross-tenant impact until full routing changes at 06:50 UTC.

Analysis highlights: 
- Attribution: signal correlation between per-tenant KV cache miss rate and per-tenant token consumption shows the noisy tenant accounted for ~44% of cache misses while only consuming ~22% of reserved capacity.
- Reservation mismatch: our reservation sizing logic assumes stable working set; this workload had a sudden working-set growth causing reservation under-provisioning and aggressive use of burst credits.
- Burst policy gaps: the burst-credit slabs are too coarse; a single large consumer can exhaust credits for adjacent tenants before decay kicks in.

Proposed action items (owner + ETA):
1) Soft-fence controller prototype (owner: Marco Chen, ETA: 2025-11-30): implement a controller that creates transient soft-fences based on per-tenant KV cache miss rate, hot-shard detection, and a short-term credit burn rate threshold. Soft-fences should be reversible and emit audit events. Acceptance criteria: reduces cross-tenant KV miss correlation by >= 60% in canary.
2) Burst-credit slab recalibration (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2025-12-04): replace current fixed slabs with a percentile-based adaptive slab that factors in recent working-set volatility. Acceptance criteria: median recovery time after synthetic noisy spikes falls below 120s in staging.
3) Reservation sanity checks (owner: Diego Morales, ETA: 2025-12-02): add pre-allocation validators that detect sudden working-set growth and temporarily increase soft-reservations for impacted tenants while signaling billing/alerts. Acceptance criteria: no eviction churn observed during staged synthetic shocks.
4) KV-cache observability and attribution (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2025-11-26): add per-tenant KV cache miss attribution drilldowns in Console and a lightweight trace that ties miss spikes to request hashes. Acceptance criteria: actionable tenant-level attribution visible in Console and referenced in incident playbook.
5) Runbook and automated rollback (owner: SRE Team, ETA: 2025-11-28): update playbook to include soft-fence steps, telemetry checks, and rollback commands. Acceptance criteria: runbook validated in a scheduled chaos exercise.

Rollout plan: deploy soft-fence controller to canary pool (10% of dedicated clusters) with metrics gated rollout. Run three synthetic noise injections per cluster during canary window and validate KPIs. If stable, roll to 50% then 100% within two weeks.

Measurement & KPIs: track per-tenant KV miss correlation, cluster-level eviction rate, median P95 tail latency for non-noisy tenants, and time-to-recovery after injected noise. Dashboards and SLOs to be recorded in the incident board.

Risks & trade-offs: soft-fencing can temporarily throttle customer throughput; mitigation: make fences soft (non-destructive), provide clear audit logs and automatic expiry. Adaptive slabs increase complexity in billing reconciliation — finance and billing teams must validate.

Dependencies: requires allocator changes (ENG-314159), Console telemetry work (PM-50123), and billing reconciliation sign-off.

Notes: keep customer communication minimal until playbook finalized. SOC/security review not needed for controller prototype, but audit logging must be retained for compliance.
